response: Prompting primary care providers about increased patient risk as a result of family history does not appear to be effective in improving their ability to identify patients at high risk for common conditions. According to the available data, instituting simple, at-the-visit family history prompts did not result in any significant change. The results suggest that further studies are needed to examine physicians' perception of the utility of prompts for family history risk, as the current approach may not be sufficient to improve risk identification.
